item.title: OXE-AugE: A Large-Scale Robot Augmentation of OXE for Scaling Cross-Embodiment Policy Learning
item.description:
Generalist robot policies must control many arm and gripper combinations, but recollecting data and retraining for each new robot is too costly. The widely used Open X-Embodiment dataset gathers over sixty robot datasets yet is badly imbalanced: the top four robot types make up over 85% of its real data. item.title: Coupling Execution Horizon and Sampling Depth in Flow-Matching VLA Policies
item.description:

item.title: Revisiting Temporal Regularization for Smooth Control in Deep Reinforcement Learning
item.description:

Existing methods directly limit how much actions change when the input state changes slightly, but these broad constraints hurt task performance as smoothing grows. item.title: BitVLA: 1-bit Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotics Manipulation
item.description:
Vision-language-action models are too large for the edge devices robots carry. Rather than compressing after training, BitVLA uses extreme low-bit weights from the start: every parameter is one of minus one, zero or one, about 1.58 bits, conventionally called a 1-bit model, built on the open BitNet LLM.
